pr_title: fix(core): support sanitizing uncontained `<tr>` and `<td>` elements
pr_body:
Previously, `<tr>` or `<td>`elements that were not containing within a
`<table>` element were stripped from the string by the HTML sanitizer.

Fixes #35387

---

This PR looks more complicated than it really is. First of all there is a simple rename refactoring in the first commit The second commit contains the actual fix. It looks busy but here is the overview.

Previously the inert element was worked out like this:

- If DOMParser strategy is available use that; if it fails mid-computation fall back to the inert body strategy.
- In the inert body strategy
  - first try putting the content into a `<template>` element; if that works use it
  - otherwise fallback on putting the content into a special `<body>` element attached to an inert document.

The problem is that neither the DOMParser nor the inert document body will accept HTML fragments, such as an unwrapped `<tr>` element. This PR just moves the order around a bit. Now the inert element is worked out as:

- First try putting the content into a `<template>` element; if that works use it
- If DOMParser strategy is available use that; if it fails mid-computation fall back to the inert body strategy.
- Fallback on putting the content into a special `<body>` element attached to an inert document.

Note that what has happened is that the priority of the `<template>` element as the container for the inert content has increased ahead of the other two strategies.

**We need to review this from a security perspective to ensure that putting `<template>` strategy first does not open up any attack vectors for all the browsers that we support.**

@koto it would be great if you could take a view.
pr_comments: Didn't we default to DOMParser to workaround a Firefox issue in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/36578 ?

> Didn't we default to DOMParser to workaround a Firefox issue in #36578 ?

That is a good point @koto - thanks for the reminder. Also I spoke with @cure53 at DOMPuriify and he pointed out other potential vulnerabilities of relying on `<template>` over the `DOMParser`.

I have identified a fairly straightforward workaround for the application developer: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-2yrwc7?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.ts.  So I will close this and the issue as won't fix.

OK I looked into the details of the issue. The original problem (still present in FF - https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1205631) makes the DOMParser the safer option in sanitizers that keep svg and leave contents of the style nodes. Angular's sanitizer has neither of those features for now (https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/542ba1fc0018f5d8fa4f5d92587b8ec8b5a3adb1/packages/core/src/sanitization/html_sanitizer.ts#L87-L102) - this is why the mxss test still passes, and the resulting nodes are safe. I also tested the PR on various new mxss based on MathML and SVG. Everything seems to be still secure, but with mxss you just never know, as it's very sensitive to the allowlist of elements and attributes.

If you decide to keep this PR (there's no security issues with it now, so I'm OK with it), could you add a comment to rigorously test for mxss when anything around style, svg and mathml nodes changes?

It does sound though like a better way forward is to keep the DOMParser logic and workaround for the element wrapping in the applications themselves, sanitizing invalid HTML fragments is a misfeature IMHO.

issue_context.title: sanitizeHTML incorrectly strips <tr> (and more tags) in IE, FF, Edge
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by package `@angular/core` ### Is this a regression? I cannot tell. But appears already in v. 8 on stackblitz. ### Description `sanitizeHtml` (or binding to `[innerHtml]`) strips out `` or other table related tags in Firefox, Internet Explorer, Edge. ~But working in Chrome.~ **Edit:** As of Angular 11.1.2 not working in Chrome anymore. It can be demonstrated by following: ```
``` Seems the problem lies in `getInertBodyElement_DOMParser` which tries to parse the content into DOM, but directly adds the content into `body`, while adding `` into body is invalid in some browsers, resulting in stripping the elements. Additionaly, no warning about stripped content is produced, because this happens before calling the `sanitizer` itself in `_sanitizeHtml` ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction [https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-qbswrh?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-qbswrh?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html) Open in Firefox. Angular 11 stopped working in Chrome as well: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-zrwgse?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html ```
``` ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:**

comments: [**@smile2014**](https://github.com/smile2014) The value passed to `[innerHTML]` can't contain any Angular binding. There isn't any compiler that would compile it in AOT mode.

This issue now affects chrome as well (a regression somewhere around Angular 11.1.2)
https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-zrwgse?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.html

I think the fact it is now also doing this on Chrome is caused by the fact that we now use the `DOMParser` to sanitize HTML in Chrome as well as other browsers. And AFAICT: ```ts const body = new window.DOMParser().parseFromString('Hello{{value}}', 'text/html').body; ``` results in a `body` element where these `tr` and `td` tags are stripped.

I think this is because `<tr>` elements are not valid outside of a table.
A workaround would be to ensure that any innerHTML strings that you want to be sanitized is valid HTML on its own.

So having looked into a potential fix for this, I have decided that this is too problematic to try to do in a generic way.
This is also the case for the leading sanitizer DOMPurify, which suggests that you work around this by using "hooks".


Angular sanitization does not have hooks but you can still work around this. Here is an example: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-2yrwc7?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.ts

Note that the inner table string is still sanitized as expected but the `<tr>` and `<td>` are not stripped.

Since this can be worked around fairly easily, and that there is no reliable fix that can be done generically inside the sanitizer, I am going to close this.

review_comments: Despite this PR, browsers that do not support the `<template>` strategy still have the problem with unwrapped `<tr>` etc elements. In terms of browsers, I believe this is only IE11 now.

Both results are safe HTML and we don't really care which is returned, so there is no real need to select a result based on sniffing here. (In fact only checking `isDOMParserAvailable()` is no longer sufficient.
